boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Lewis & Clark spaces with documented ways students study, meet, eat, or spend time together.

cards.title: Aubrey R. Watzek Library
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate Campus
cards.notes: Use the quiet areas for focused work or arrange a group session; the library provides study space, technology, and reservable rooms.
cards.short_summary: A campus-center library built for both quiet work and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark says Watzek Library offers spaces for quiet study, group work, and access to technology.
cards.source_title: Academic Services and Resources — Undergraduate Catalog
cards.access_notes: Library access and room-reservation rules may vary by term; check the library before visiting.

cards.title: Trail Room
cards.subtitle: Fowler Student Center
cards.notes: Choose a table for a study break, a casual meetup, or a meal; the venue has seating intended for studying, relaxing, and meeting.
cards.short_summary: A renovated Fowler Student Center dining space with room to linger.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark states that the Trail Room has seating and spaces for students to study, relax, or meet with friends.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require payment or an applicable meal plan; consult current dining hours before going.

cards.title: The Dovecote
cards.subtitle: Albany Quadrangle
cards.notes: Stop at the Albany Quadrangle coffee shop, then use the patio seating when conditions are suitable for an outdoor conversation or break.
cards.short_summary: A campus coffee shop with documented outdoor patio seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark identifies the Dovecote in Albany Quadrangle and notes that students use its outdoor patio seating on sunny days.
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for café items; patio availability is weather-dependent.

cards.title: Fields Dining Room
cards.subtitle: Fowler Student Center
cards.notes: Plan a meal meetup here when the dining hall is serving; it is the undergraduate campus’s main dining hall for three daily meal periods.
cards.short_summary: The main undergraduate dining hall for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark describes Fields Dining Room as its main undergraduate-campus dining hall, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
cards.access_notes: Entry and meals require payment or an applicable meal plan; confirm current service hours.

cards.title: Council Chamber Foyer
cards.subtitle: Fowler Student Center
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or reading and use the foyer seating as an alternate study location when you want a change from the library.
cards.short_summary: A named Fowler study alternative beside the Council Chamber.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark Student Life lists seats in the Council Chamber Foyer as an additional campus location for virtual classes or study.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared student-center area; avoid using it when programming or events need the surrounding space.

cards.title: Munger Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Center of Templeton
cards.notes: Use the courtyard as an outdoor change of scene for virtual classwork or reading, and bring weather-appropriate layers and headphones.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Templeton courtyard identified for studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark Student Life lists Munger Courtyard in the center of Templeton as an additional location for virtual classes or study.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions affect comfort and availability.

cards.title: Albany Quadrangle Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Albany Quadrangle
cards.notes: Set up at a courtyard bench for a brief study session or virtual class, then move indoors if weather or noise changes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor academic-quad option for independent work.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark Student Life lists benches in the Albany Quadrangle courtyard as an additional location for virtual classes or study.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating is weather-dependent; nearby Albany offices and services have separate access rules.

cards.title: Fir Acres Amphitheatre
cards.subtitle: Between Evans Music Center and Fir Acres Theatre
cards.notes: Use the outdoor amphitheater for reading or a virtual class when it is not programmed; choose a seat that keeps walkways clear.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor study alternative between music and theatre buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark Student Life lists the outdoor amphitheater between Evans and Fir Acres as an additional location for virtual classes or study.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use depends on weather and scheduled campus activity.

cards.title: BoDine
cards.subtitle: BoDine/Biology-Psychology area
cards.notes: Look for the covered benches in the BoDine and Biology-Psychology area when you need a sheltered outdoor place for classwork or reading.
cards.short_summary: A covered-bench study stop near science and mathematics buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark Student Life lists covered benches in the BoDine/BioPsych area as an additional location for virtual classes or study.
cards.access_notes: The benches are outdoors; respect adjacent instructional and research activity.

cards.title: Estate Gardens
cards.subtitle: East of Frank Manor House
cards.notes: Walk the garden terraces for a short outdoor reset, staying on open paths and following any posted directions around ongoing landscape work.
cards.short_summary: Historic terraced gardens descending from Frank Manor House.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis & Clark describes the Estate Gardens as four terraces sloping from Frank Manor House toward the former rose garden.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted access guidance; portions of the lower gardens have had renovation-related restrictions.
